name: Per-element sidechain shapes: bass ducks the whole kick, mids/highs duck only the punch, depth set by loudness, multiband for full-range sounds
goal: Set sidechain ducking per element instead of one kick-shaped duck on everything: the bass and low end duck deeply for the whole kick length (returning exactly as the tail ends), mid/high instruments duck only briefly around the kick's punch/transient, and loud foreground layers duck deeper than quiet background layers. Full-range sounds such as a reese use multiband sidechain with separate low and mid/high shapes. Don't fix pumping by lowering the mix knob, because partial ducking leaves kick and element overlapping and that shared volume hits the master limiter early. Delta vs the generic sidechain-compressor-duck-synth-pads skill: shape and depth rules per element and the loudness/limiter reason.

source.title: Sidechain Tutorials Ruined A Generation of Producers
source.transcript_note: Show-transcript text; mentorship/application promo section dropped. The video gives no numeric ms/% values beyond 50% vs 100% mix; times below are left to ears/kick length.

prerequisites: A DAW with volume-shaping sidechain (shaper/LFO-tool or compressor keyed from the kick)
A multiband sidechain/shaper for full-range sounds (the video uses a free multiband sidechain plugin)
A master limiter to test the result

inputs.name: elements
inputs.description: Bass, leads, pads, vocals and so on, each with a role (low end vs mid/high) and a loudness (foreground vs background)

outputs.name: per_element_duck_settings
outputs.description: For each element: duck shape (full-kick vs punch-only), depth/mix, and band split if multiband

constraints: No universal numbers given in the source: derive the duck length from your kick's actual length
Don't use the mix/depth knob to hide a wrong shape; fix the shape first, then set depth
Not affiliated with the creator or plugin vendors; works with any shaper/compressor sidechain

steps.action: Split the kick mentally into punch (transient/click/attack, the only part with mid/high energy) and tail (mostly low end). Check the kick's total length.
steps.expect: You know the punch duration and the tail end time

steps.action: On the bass/low end, draw a deep duck (high mix/depth, near full) that lasts the whole kick and returns right as the kick tail ends: not before, not way after. A longer kick needs a longer duck.
steps.expect: Kick and bass never sound at the same time in the lows

steps.action: On mid and high instruments (leads, synths, pads, vocals to an extent), use a short duck that covers only the kick's punch and then recovers quickly.
steps.expect: The aggressive 'yanked out' pumping disappears; synths stay present during the kick tail

steps.action: Set depth by loudness. Loud, important foreground layers get deeper, more precise ducks (they pump a bit more); quiet background layers can duck less.
steps.expect: The loudest overlaps with the kick are removed first

steps.action: For a sound with lows plus mids/highs (for example a reese bass), use multiband sidechain: a long, deep full-kick shape on the low band and a short punch-only shape on the mid/high band.
steps.expect: The low band clears for the kick tail while the bass's upper content keeps moving

steps.action: Avoid partial ducking (for example a 50% mix) as a cure for pumping: the element stays on top of the kick, their summed volume makes peaks, and across many elements it buries the kick.
steps.expect: Elements actually get out of the kick's way at its moments of overlap

steps.action: Test into a master limiter: raise the input to the fixed ceiling and compare against the old setting.
steps.expect: The limiter clamps later and less at kick hits, so the track gets louder before squashing, and the kick stays audible

verification: Gain-reduction meter on the master limiter shows less reduction at kick hits than with the one-shape/50% setup at the same loudness
The bass duck ends within a few ms of the kick tail end
A/B listening: no audible pumping on the leads/pads, kick still clear
